thought.text: Let me restart the key jobs with `setsid` (so they survive independent of my command's process group), leveraging the warm caches:

reasoning_content:
State check:
- Keycloak, meilisearch, postgres images have been pulled. localstack is in progress.
- pnpm store: 811MB already downloaded (killed before install completed, but store is warm — re-running pnpm install will be much faster).
- Dev servers are run on the host via `nx serve`.

Now the plan:
1. Rebuild the backend image using a warm cache mount — Maven Central is currently responsive (3/3 OK, fast). This will verify whether the token works with the dummy.
2. In parallel: complete pnpm install (warm store).
3. Continue pulling the remaining compose images (localstack, mailpit, imgproxy, python, nginx).
4. After that, run `just up --detach` (documented method) to bring up the full stack, then `just serve` for the dev server (or full `just up`).

Important: `just up` will be run as a foreground command with a 600-second timeout. The remaining steps are: pnpm install (store is warm, but linking 2000+ packages + the prepare script that generates the OpenAPI client — may still take a few minutes), image build (warm cache — just re-fetching the failed artifacts), compose create (build — cache hit), up -d --wait (image is pulled; keycloak's cold start is about 125 seconds), seeding (a few minutes?).

`just up` is a long-running interactive-style command (it keeps running while the dev server is up). The guide says `--detach` skips the dev server and exits. That is a documented method of the guide ("`just up` also accepts `--detach` (skips starting the dev server)"). After that, `just serve` can be run to start the dev server (also documented in the recipe table).

Actually, for "installing" the software, a stack that has been brought up with `--detach` and then verified via URL is a solid installation. The dev server (app/cms/boards) is part of "everything," so try to get it running too via `just serve` (in the background, monitored).

So, kick off the backend rebuild right now with the warm cache (background, nohup, its own process group — use setsid to avoid the previous pitfall of the entire group being killed by the timeout).

Important lesson: the previous foreground build got killed at 600 seconds and took the whole process group down with it (the nohup'd background docker build was also killed). So now: run the long build in the background with setsid + nohup, and poll it with short commands.

Let's start:
1. setsid nohup docker build backend
2. setsid nohup pnpm install
3. setsid nohup docker pull of the remaining images

After that, poll in 600-second chunks.

action.command:
cd /workspace/backend
rm -f /tmp/backend-build2.log
setsid nohup env GITHUB_TOKEN="ghp_dummytesttoken0000000000000000000000" docker build \
  --secret id=github_token,env=GITHUB_TOKEN \
  -f docker/spring/Dockerfile \
  -t urbo-backend-test \
  . > /tmp/backend-build2.log 2>&1 < /dev/null &
echo "backend build pid $!"

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments:
{"command": "cd /workspace/backend
rm -f /tmp/backend-build2.log
setsid nohup env GITHUB_TOKEN="ghp_dummytesttoken0000000000000000000000" docker build \
  --secret id=github_token,env=GITHUB_TOKEN \
  -f docker/spring/Dockerfile \
  -t urbo-backend-test \
  . > /tmp/backend-build2.log 2>&1 < /dev/null &
echo "backend build pid $!"", "summary": "Restart backend build with warm cache"}

summary: Restart backend build with warm cache
